574adaca39fa99c1.what: Systematic benchmark of MACE potentials for chemically disordered bcc/fcc Fe–Ni alloys. A system-specific MACE–sqs model, trained on spin-polarized PBE data for special quasirandom structures, reaches validation errors of 2.0 meV/atom (energy) and 24.3 meV/Å (forces). It is compared with several MACE foundation models.
574adaca39fa99c1.why: To define where targeted training beats broad foundation models for alloys with magnetic effects.
574adaca39fa99c1.how: Spin-polarized DFT on SQS spanning composition, volume and shear. Models are compared on equations of state, cubic elastic constants and thermal expansion.
574adaca39fa99c1.impact: Directly relevant to the InGaAs alloy project (self-trained Deep Potential vs MACE across compositions) and to MLIP failure-mode analysis. The finding that no model is uniformly best, and that magnetism is only implicit, is a useful template for comparing MLIPs on alloy κ in the Phonon Olympics.

88ba3518521e4999.what: Reports glass-like, ultralow thermal conductivity (0.21 W/mK at 20 K) in the ordered quasi-1D crystal (Nb4Se15I2)I2. Heat capacity and Raman show a boson-peak-like excess of low-energy states. AIMD shows strongly anharmonic, anisotropic motion of interchain I- ions, and phonon calculations show acoustic–optical avoided crossing.
88ba3518521e4999.why: To understand how an ordered crystal can show glassy heat transport and how boson-peak-like excess relates to it.
88ba3518521e4999.how: Thermal conductivity, heat-capacity and low-frequency Raman measurements, combined with AIMD, phonon calculations and a minimal theory of hybridization with anharmonic interchain modes.
88ba3518521e4999.impact: Relevant to lattice-dynamics and anharmonicity methods in the BTE projects (e.g. BaTiO3 and SrTiO3 defect phonons). It is a mechanism case where the standard phonon-gas BTE picture may fail, so it is useful for thinking about the limits of BTE.

8fbb86e98032c5eb.what: First-principles study of UN and UO2 combining DFT+U, three-phonon BTE for lattice κ and electron–phonon-limited transport (SERTA vs CRTA). UO2 is lattice-dominated, with κL falling from 7.7 to 2.4 W/mK over 300–1000 K. UN is electron-dominated, with electronic κ rising from 12.9 to 31.6 W/mK over 300–1500 K.
8fbb86e98032c5eb.why: The relative electron and phonon contributions to heat transport in these nuclear fuels are unresolved.
8fbb86e98032c5eb.how: DFT+U with magnetic configurations (NM, FM, AFM), three-phonon BTE, and electron–phonon self-energy relaxation-time approximation. No fit to thermal-conductivity data.
8fbb86e98032c5eb.impact: Methodologically close to the phonon BTE workflow (phono3py/ALAMODE-type) and shows the value of SERTA over CRTA when electrons matter. It is not directly tied to a current project; it is only loosely transferable to the metallic/doped cases.

74a4b6518b286bc9.what: Review of how composite architectures (porous structures, nanoprecipitates, magnetic phases, crystalline–amorphous hybrids, superlattices) suppress lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectrics. It covers phonon theory, AMM/DMM interface models, mean-field theory and device-level issues such as non-uniform heat fields and thermal expansion mismatch.
74a4b6518b286bc9.why: To suppress lattice κ with secondary phases and interfaces without degrading electronic transport.
74a4b6518b286bc9.how: Literature review with benchmarks across temperature regimes and design principles.
74a4b6518b286bc9.impact: Background on AMM/DMM and interface scattering relevant to the interfacial transport work (GaN/Al2O3, BAs interfaces). Mostly experimental and thermoelectric-focused, so moderate relevance as a reference.

aaeedd1a887bc13e.what: Measures cross-plane thermal conductivity of ultrathin (<30 nm) PEALD BeO films on GaN-on-Al2O3 and Si using FDTR, a series-resistor model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Values are about 20 W/mK (single-crystalline) and 12 W/mK (nanocrystalline). Device thermal modeling shows sc-BeO as a top-side heat spreader reduces device thermal resistance.
aaeedd1a887bc13e.why: High-κ insulators near the channel could improve heat removal in transistors, but ultrathin BeO transport was unexplored.
aaeedd1a887bc13e.how: FDTR measurement, diffusive series resistor model, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and device thermal modeling. Total resistance data are consistent with a ballistic transport model.
aaeedd1a887bc13e.impact: Related to the GaN/AlGaN HEMT multiscale thermal modeling project: the device modeling of a BeO heat spreader on GaN and the ballistic-transport consistency give data for validation. The work is mainly experimental, so relevance is moderate.

7609801c77ab4a3c.what: DFT and AIMD study of Cs2CdMCl6 (M = Mg, Si, Ge, Sn) double halide perovskites: structural, mechanical, electronic (HSE06 gaps 2.13–4.27 eV), optical and phonon properties. All are dynamically stable except Cs2CdSnCl6, and AIMD at 300 K for 5 ps shows no significant distortion.
7609801c77ab4a3c.why: To find stable lead-free perovskites for optoelectronics.
7609801c77ab4a3c.how: GGA-PBE/PBEsol and HSE06 DFT, phonon dispersions and 5 ps AIMD at 300 K.
7609801c77ab4a3c.impact: Low relevance. It uses only standard DFT and phonon stability checks and has no thermal-transport calculation.

869a2664b859ff1e.what: Shows a physics-based linear correlation mapping coverage-dependent adsorption energies on metal surfaces to gas-phase pairwise (Mie potential) interactions, explained by bond-order conservation. It generalizes across facets and adsorbate classes and agrees with CO/Pt(111) calorimetry.
869a2664b859ff1e.why: Lateral interactions on crowded catalyst surfaces are hard to compute and ML methods need large data sets and lack interpretability.
869a2664b859ff1e.how: First-principles adsorption energies correlated against Mie-potential gas-phase interactions.
869a2664b859ff1e.impact: Low relevance. Catalysis-specific; only a general example of a physically interpretable descriptor in place of a data-hungry ML model.

06922282d97fbdda.what: First-principles study of the electronic structure and thermoelectric transport of the hybrid double perovskite (CH3NH3)2AgBiCl6. No abstract text was provided.
06922282d97fbdda.how: First-principles calculations (details not stated in the abstract).
06922282d97fbdda.impact: Low relevance; no abstract and no sign of lattice-dynamics or MLIP methods relevant to current projects.

3d928bd2163dded8.what: LitMOF is an LLM multi-agent framework that reads the original publication for each MOF structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry. It produced LitMOF-DB with 189,567 computation-ready structures, including 9,277 repaired entries, and recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks.
3d928bd2163dded8.why: Nearly half of MOF database entries contain structural errors that propagate into screening and ML workflows.
3d928bd2163dded8.how: Multi-agent LLM pipeline applied to the CSD MOF subset. A direct air capture screening case study shows how errors distort adsorption energies and selectivity.
3d928bd2163dded8.impact: Not about thermal transport, but a concrete example of LLM agents curating atomistic data, which is relevant to automated workflows and to training-data quality for MLIPs (e.g. the AlGaN pipeline).

d948d88e61c4754d.what: Adds 2,2'-biimidazole to MeO-2PACz self-assembled monolayers to improve perovskite quality and interfacial charge transport, reaching 25.59% efficiency, and 23.03% for a 1.68 eV wide-bandgap inverted cell.
d948d88e61c4754d.why: Additive-mediated SAM enhancement regulates perovskite crystallization and interface charge transport.
d948d88e61c4754d.how: Additive incorporation into SAM precursors, with theoretical and experimental characterization and device fabrication.
d948d88e61c4754d.impact: Low relevance. Experimental perovskite solar cell work with no phonon or thermal content.

f7ff6e22a64097f7.what: Introduces KinTree, an interpretable decision-tree framework for kinetic modeling of atomistic simulations. It uses noncovalent-interaction features and a unified kinetic-structural objective to produce Markovian state decompositions from raw trajectories.
f7ff6e22a64097f7.why: Markov state models are opaque and need post hoc analysis to link states to physical interactions.
f7ff6e22a64097f7.how: Decision-tree architecture on interaction features, validated by Chapman–Kolmogorov tests across several molecular systems.
f7ff6e22a64097f7.impact: Low-to-moderate relevance. A biomolecular application, but the interpretable, feature-based analysis of MD trajectories is conceptually related to MLIP interpretability and latent-space analysis.

5336abbeec915949.what: Builds a rattlesnake-inspired NIR sensor using photothermal conversion at Au@ITO–graphite asymmetric electrodes with an ionogel. It produces an open-circuit voltage at near-zero temperature gradient, with about 70 times the sensitivity of symmetric electrodes.
5336abbeec915949.why: Conventional NIR sensing materials are limited by conversion efficiency, cooling volume and recyclability.
5336abbeec915949.how: Au nanoparticle LSPR heating, asymmetric ion adsorption/desorption at the electrode–electrolyte interface, 0.1 mm spacing, array demonstrations.
5336abbeec915949.impact: Low relevance. Experimental sensor device with no connection to phonon transport or the listed projects.

ffdf711d1e7c549f.what: cuEquivariance v0.14.0 extends optimized Triangle Multiplicative Update kernels to continuous ranges of shapes. It adds the first TriMul kernels for B300 and GB300 and Vera Rubin support, plus new Triangle Attention forward kernels for Torch and JAX.
ffdf711d1e7c549f.why: The 0.13 optimized inference kernels only covered a fixed list of exact shapes.
ffdf711d1e7c549f.how: Prebuilt kernels in the wheel with no JIT, BF16 inputs, and an N and batch range that depends on the class.
ffdf711d1e7c549f.impact: Mostly targets AlphaFold-style triangle operations. The library supports equivariant networks such as MACE, but these release notes do not mention MLIP kernels. Low relevance to the JAX/CUDA HPC work.

842f4f75613083b4.what: cuEquivariance v0.13.0 adds optimized prebuilt TriMul kernels for stated shapes (inference and training on H100/H200/GH200/B200/RTX PRO 6000), mask=None for JAX triangle attention, and bug fixes including a PyTorch 2.14 training failure.
842f4f75613083b4.why: To speed up triangle operations and fix kernel regressions and errors.
842f4f75613083b4.how: CUDA 13 wheels only. Supported PyTorch versions are 2.11–2.13. Shapes outside the validated list use the 0.12 implementation.
842f4f75613083b4.impact: Low relevance. The notes concern triangle-operation kernels, not the MLIP tensor-product kernels used with MACE. Note only if you rely on cuEquivariance JAX/CUDA.

3b7c8e5708a41e1d.what: Semiconductor Engineering's technical-paper roundup of Nov. 25 lists papers including 3D-NAND-CIM analog in-memory compute, chiplet matching for yield, HBF for GPU systems, backside clock mesh in BSPDN, and LLM agents for cryptographic hardware.
3b7c8e5708a41e1d.how: A list of titles and research organizations only.
3b7c8e5708a41e1d.impact: Low relevance. No thermal-focused paper in this list, though BSPDN and heterogeneous integration are background for electronics thermal trends.

92b5001709e879cd.what: Article arguing that multi-die systems need a system-level data-movement architecture (traffic management, QoS, routing, observability) beyond a die-to-die controller and PHY.
92b5001709e879cd.why: Treating each die boundary independently raises integration and verification effort and reduces chiplet reuse.
92b5001709e879cd.how: Architecture discussion based on the separation of transport (controller/PHY) from system architecture.
92b5001709e879cd.impact: Low relevance. Chiplet architecture trend with no thermal content in the excerpt.

4decc83470dcf5f0.what: Describes Siemens Avery UCIe VIP for verifying UCIe 4.0 features with compliance tests, protocol-aware monitoring, transaction recording, scoreboarding and error-injection callbacks.
4decc83470dcf5f0.why: To show that state transitions, error handling and recovery are correct in UCIe 4.0 designs.
4decc83470dcf5f0.how: A verification plan derived from the exact UCIe revision and supported options.
4decc83470dcf5f0.impact: Low relevance. Verification tooling with no thermal or materials content.

f2c82b71ec31237f.what: Article on using agentic AI to speed up custom silicon for physical AI (robots), arguing agents need persistent design context, such as a design ontology covering RTL, verification, synthesis, timing and PPA.
f2c82b71ec31237f.why: AI models evolve faster than conventional tape-out cycles, so design development speed is the constraint.
f2c82b71ec31237f.how: Three stated requirements for agentic AI; only the first (persistent design context) is visible in the excerpt.
f2c82b71ec31237f.impact: Low relevance. Mainly an analogy for agent workflows with persistent context, which is relevant in spirit to automated first-principles/lattice-dynamics agents, but it has no thermal content in the excerpt.

c28905b42e76756e.what: BluGlass is extending its visible GaN laser roadmap to surface-emitting lasers, citing a provisional patent application for a GaN-based photonic-crystal surface-emitting laser (PCSEL) platform.
c28905b42e76756e.why: To add a new product platform complementing its edge-emitting lasers.
c28905b42e76756e.how: Builds on in-house epitaxy, device design, fabrication and optical mode control.
c28905b42e76756e.impact: Low relevance. GaN optoelectronics, not power/RF HEMT thermal modeling.

ff0fdbc8578a5b9c.what: lanl/ALF is an open-source active learning framework for training machine-learned interatomic potentials, with topics including uncertainty quantification.
ff0fdbc8578a5b9c.how: Python library; no other details given in the provided text.
ff0fdbc8578a5b9c.impact: Directly relevant to the active-learning MLIP work (boron arsenide, AlGaN pipeline) and data-efficiency questions. Worth checking which MLIP backends it supports and how it estimates uncertainty.

d8aa580497087634.what: Article reporting mixed results when chipmakers apply AI to derivative and new chip designs, with outputs differing from expectations and costing more, and with gaps in multi-physics simulation, data and verification limiting end-to-end automation.
d8aa580497087634.why: AI-assisted reuse depends on complete design data, which may sit at foundries, OSATs and equipment providers.
d8aa580497087634.how: Industry interviews, for example Keysight EDA's general manager.
d8aa580497087634.impact: Low-to-moderate relevance. Cites missing multi-physics simulation as a bottleneck, which supports the case for fast thermal simulation in industry roles.

2fc7e645df4b4cd2.what: py-MCMD is a Python code that sets up hybrid MD/MC (NAMD/GOMC) simulations for NVT, NPT, GCMC and GEMC-NVT ensembles.
2fc7e645df4b4cd2.how: Python wrapper around NAMD and GOMC.
2fc7e645df4b4cd2.impact: Low relevance. Classical MD/MC for chemistry; the workflow does not use LAMMPS or MLIPs.

17470dc912ad2b6d.what: ASME SHTC 2027 will be held August 1–4, 2027 at the Hilton Orlando, FL. The abstract deadline is December 8, 2026, with notification on December 22, 2026. Tracks include Nanoscale Thermal Transport, Computational Heat Transfer, AI/ML & Data-Driven Thermal Sciences and Heat Transfer in Electronic Equipment.
17470dc912ad2b6d.why: A call for abstracts for a broad heat and mass transfer conference.
17470dc912ad2b6d.how: Abstract submission through the conference website by December 8, 2026.
17470dc912ad2b6d.impact: Good fit for the phonon BTE / JAX-BTE and GaN HEMT work in the Nanoscale Thermal Transport or Heat Transfer in Electronic Equipment tracks. It is held in the US and you presented at SHTC 2025, so submitting is worthwhile; the deadline is in about 2 weeks.

1670117f9cf82412.what: ASTFE homepage was updated. The visible events are the 10th BSME Thermo-Fluid Engineering conference (December 19–21, 2026, Dhaka) and a January 2027 event whose name is truncated. The page lists no TFEC dates or deadlines.
1670117f9cf82412.why: Not stated in the page excerpt.
1670117f9cf82412.how: No submission format or deadline given.
1670117f9cf82412.impact: Low relevance now. No US TFEC date was found, and the listed events are not US-held. Recheck later for TFEC dates.
